They partly can't: the same-morning IndexNow push covers Bing (so ChatGPT), and Google's index covers AI Overviews, but Claude reads Brave's index, which nothing in the ledger touches. Meanwhile Perplexity's source pool is small enough that a single well-structured local page can win a citation. Six honest Q&As per town and service page (cost range, lead time, half-round vs K-style, guard options, who covers this borough) is exactly the shape these engines quote, and 'who installs copper gutters in York PA' is a low-competition question where a York County one-owner shop can plausibly be the named answer instead of Angi.

For Perplexity, <cite index="14-1">its source pool is smaller and more curated, so a single well-structured page from a local business can appear in answer cards if it directly answers the query and looks fresh</cite>, with concrete instructions to <cite index="14-14,14-16">add FAQPage schema with at least six questions per page and update the page every 30–45 days with a visible last-updated timestamp</cite> (https://www.pleiadesconsultancy.com/blog/how-to-get-cited-by-perplexity-ai-2026). Schema payoff is measurable: <cite index="15-10,15-11">pages with FAQ schema are reported 2.8x more likely to be cited in AI answers, and the core stack for a local service business is LocalBusiness + Service + Review + FAQPage + Organization</cite> (https://evolveamz.com/local-business-ai-search-guide/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Check robots.txt and server logs for Bravebot access, then submit nemoseamlessgutter.com to Brave Search's webmaster/index submission form today — a 10-minute job that no competing York gutter shop has done.
effort: days
cost: free
expected: Brave crawl confirmed and site submitted; FAQPage schema (6+ real Q&As, no invented prices or credentials) validating on 9+ pages; visible last-updated dates. Success at 60 days = NEMO named or cited in 3 of 10 manual test prompts ('who installs half round copper gutters in York PA', 'gutter guard cost York County') across Claude and Perplexity, and the AI-answer-engine visitor count off zero for the first time.

last_scout.notes: Order of operations: the photo-text offer first (hours, free, aimed straight at the weakest number), Brave submission second (10 minutes, nobody local has done it), local links third because they take weeks. TIMING MATTERS RIGHT NOW — it is 31 July. York County leaf-fall guard and cleaning work is decided in August and early September; every dollar and hour spent before Labor Day is worth more than the same effort in November, and mid-winter is when to write pages, not chase bookings. THE HONEST DIAGNOSIS OF 300 VIEWS / 0 CALLS: the profile is probably not being skipped for ranking reasons alone. 4.2 stars on 13 reviews reads as 'a few unhappy customers' to a homeowner comparing three options. Do not touch that number with anything artificial. The fix is the ledger's existing review candidate plus replying publicly and calmly to every negative review — <cite index="5-8">recency, frequency, the specific words customers use, and whether the owner responds all affect local results</cite>. Coaching customers to name the actual service ('replaced our half-round copper on Beaver Street') is legitimate and useful, since <cite index="8-11">a review naming a specific service carries more signal than 'great service'</cite>; asking them to praise, script, or omit anything is not, and never offer anything of value for a review. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: (1) Paid AEO services that promise AI citations via 'device farms' of real phones simulating browsing — one vendor sells this openly; it is fabricated engagement, it risks the profile, and a suspension costs more than this business can earn back. (2) Yext/Moz Local style blasts to 70+ directories — <cite index="26-3,26-4">practitioners report citation cleanup rarely moves the needle and recommend spending the effort on GBP activity and reviews instead</cite>, so the existing NAP candidate should stay narrow and manual. (3) Angi/HomeAdvisor paid leads — <cite index="4-4">shared with five other companies</cite>; a one-owner shop cannot win a five-way price race. (4) Putting keywords in the GBP business name ('NEMO Seamless Gutter York PA Gutter Installation') — it does move rankings, which is exactly why it is a reportable guideline violation; not worth the suspension. (5) Any paid photo-to-quote or FSM platform at $149/mo right now — the bottleneck is inbound volume, not estimating software. A phone camera and a text thread cost nothing; revisit software after there are 20 leads a month to lose. (6) Blanket texting past contacts — with one all-time booking there is no list, and unsolicited bulk SMS is illegal under the TCPA regardless. One caution on the photo offer: publish ranges, state plainly that a final price needs an on-site measure, and never let the AI agent quote a firm number.
